chapter_note: This chapter is predominantly core cosmological teaching (pentadic structure → doubling into male/female → twelvefold complex with zodiacal linkage). It is framed by a hagiographic dialogue opening and a brief doxological close. The only clear late graft is the end application that moves from cosmic antagonists to the "holy church" and sect polemic (¶8–9), which crosses from cosmos→cosmos mapping into cosmos→institution pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: Did Death arise and stand firm [...] up? Or else did it turn itself from [...] its armour [...] in its [...] but it finished [...] the two [...].
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed hagiographic dialogue frame and scene-setting: "Once again, the enlightener is sitting in the midst of his disciples, explaining to them..." and the attribution "His disciples say to him [...]".
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening scene and disciple-dialogue attribution are compilation frame. The remaining question is a substantive cosmological query about the activation of Death in the two-essences system, likely preserving the older teaching agenda beneath the frame.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] it moved it and [...] they that are in the [...] of the earth of darkness [...] first part.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary but remains within the cosmic system (earth of darkness; a numbered/ordered "part"), without institutional or citation markers.

paragraphs.core_text: Yet, after a long time, as there was not [...], it gushed and streamed up [...] the five elements of Death that gushed [...] which are smoke, fire, wind, water and darkness [...] the second time [...] they were sculpted [...] those in which Death was established [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic pentadic cosmology (five elements named) in impersonal explanatory voice; no appeal to external institutions or moral exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth part is the evil fruits [...] in the five trees that are in the five worlds of the land of darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential/pentadic mapping (fruits/trees/worlds) stays entirely within the darkness-cosmos architecture; numbered-part structure is a core marker.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth time it spread itself out to its creatures that exist in the five worlds; the ones that were formed and generated from the five fruits of Death. They are the five worlds of flesh, the five creations of darkness in which Death has been established. It spread itself out to ten parts, five male parts and five female [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree-structure teaching: five→ten (male/female doubling) described as a cosmic process of generation; still cosmos→cosmos without present-world anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, like the land of darkness, in that its spirit and its [...] they nourished the five elements [...]; this is also [how] the ten parts that are in male and female, the fire and lust of the flesh [...] them, as they yoke them with one another [...] they were established against the First Man. This is [...] of the darkness, it was condemned for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mechanistic explanation of activation (nourishing, yoking) and antagonism against the First Man—classic cosmological process discourse, not institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: Alongside the mystery of these twelve parts that came about in the darkness [...] against the First Man. The twelve [...] the twelve spirits of error that came about from the twelve signs of the zodiac [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Twelvefold extension tied to zodiacal signs remains an internal cosmological taxonomy (parts/spirits/signs) rather than church or ethical address.
Crosses the boundary from cosmic description to cosmos→institution pointing: "dwells in the holy church" anchors the antagonist pattern to the contemporary ecclesial sphere (editorial application).
Explicit church anchoring ("light that dwells in the church") plus sect-polemic functions as contemporary application rather than cosmological exposition.
Doxological closure (praise formula) functions as editorial/hagiographic framing rather than teaching content.
